I use iPhone Mirroring every day to quickly access my iPhone directly from my Mac, and this year the feature is getting even better. The public betas of iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate have rolled out this month, bringing three important updates to iPhone Mirroring. Here's everything new.

macOS 27: New Features for iPhone Mirroring

The biggest change to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now use any app compatible with iOS 27 to adjust the size of the iPhone Mirroring window. Right now, this means the feature only works with Apple's native iPhone apps. However, once developers start rolling out iOS 27 updates later, support for resizable apps will grow quickly.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only supported three preset sizes: smaller, actual size, and larger. The changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27

expected to launch later this year.

There are also several other updates to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 and iOS 27:

  • Control Center Access
  • DRM Video Support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring had no access to Control Center at all. In macOS 27, you can access it using the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut or through the View menu in your Mac's menu bar.

DRM video support means you can watch protected videos using iPhone Mirroring on your Mac. Previously, when iPhone Mirroring was enabled, all DRM-protected videos would only display a black screen.

macOS 27 has also given iPhone Mirroring a new app icon, consistent with many other built-in Apple apps.

How often do you use iPhone Mirroring on your Mac? Are you excited about these changes in iOS 27 and macOS 27? Have you tried the public beta? Let us know in the comments.
